Bill number: HB1498
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1487
 By Powers

 HOUSE BILL 1498

 By Reedy

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 16;
 Title 37 and Title 49, relative to student behavior.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) This section is known and may be cited as the "Early Behavioral Intervention

 and Reporting Act."

 (b) As used in this section, "early warning signs" means evidence of safety,

 health, or behavioral issues exhibited by a student and includes, but is not limited to,

 indicators of a student engaging in or being the victim of harassment, intimidation,

 bullying, or cyberbullying; making or receiving threats of violence; and exhibiting signs of

 substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation.

 (c) Each LEA and public charter school shall implement a computer-based

 system that teachers and school staff must use to input data of early warning signs

 demonstrated by students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school. Each LEA and

 public charter school shall ensure that each teacher and school staff member is trained

 to identify early warning signs and on how to input data into the computer-based system.

 (d) The computer-based system implemented pursuant to subsection (c) must:

 (1) Align with the harassment, intimidation, bullying, and cyberbullying

 policy adopted by the LEA in accordance with § 49-6-4503; the School Discipline

 Act, compiled in part 41 of this chapter; and with each school safety plan adopted

 by the LEA or public charter school pursuant to the Schools Against Violence in

 Education (SAVE) Act, compiled in part 8 of this chapter;

 (2) Include a database that is capable of receiving and maintaining

 student data entered by teachers and school staff on the early warning signs

 demonstrated by students; and

 (3) Immediately notify the LEA personnel serving on the LEA's threat

 assessment team created pursuant to § 49-6-2701, or the employee of the public

 charter school who is designated to receive such notification, when an early

 warning sign is entered into the system for a student.

 (e) The LEA or public charter school personnel receiving a notification of an

early warning sign of a student pursuant to subdivision (d)(3) shall review the

notification, as well as any other notifications previously received for the student, and

determine whether further action is needed to address the student's behavior.

 (f)

 (1) Each LEA and public charter school shall annually submit a report to

 the department of education that provides the following data collected by the LEA

 or public charter school in the immediately preceding school year:

 (A) The number of early warning signs input into the system;

 (B) The number of early warning signs input into the system,

 disaggregated by the number input by a:

 (i) Teacher, disaggregated further by the grade levels and

 subject areas taught by such teachers; and

 (ii) School staff, disaggregated further by the position,

 assignment, and duties of such school staff;

 (C)

 (i) The number of students for whom more than one (1)

 early warning sign was input into the system; and

 (ii) The number of early warning signs for each student for

 whom more than one (1) early warning sign input into the system;

 (D) A general description of the types of early warning signs input

 into the system; provided, that a description must not include details or

 information that would allow a student to be identified; and

 (E) A general description of the actions taken by the LEA or

 public charter school in response to each early warning sign input into the

 system; provided, that a description must not include details or

 information that would allow a student to be identified.

 (2) Reports provided pursuant to this subsection (f) must not include any

 details or information that would allow a student to be identified.

 (g) Reports made pursuant to this section must comply with the Family

Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) (20 U.S.C. § 1232g); § 10-7-504; the Data

Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, compiled in chapter 1, part 7 of this

title; and all other relevant privacy laws.

 (h) If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or public charter school is

not complying with this section, then the commissioner may withhold state funds, in an

amount determined by the commissioner, from the LEA or public charter school until the

LEA or public charter school is in compliance with this section.

 (i) Subsections (c)-(e) do not apply to an LEA or public charter school that

maintains a system for documenting early warning signs demonstrated by students that

was implemented in the LEA or public charter school before July 1, 2026; provided, that

the LEA or public charter school continuously maintains and utilizes the system.

SECTION 2. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
Beginning July 1, 2026, this bill would require each local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to use a computer-based system for teachers and school staff to record students’ “early warning signs.” These signs include safety, health, or behavioral concerns such as bullying, threats, substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal thoughts. Schools must train teachers and staff to recognize these signs and use the system. The system must align with the specified bullying, discipline, and school safety policies; keep the entered information; and immediately notify the LEA threat assessment team or a designated charter-school employee when a sign is recorded. The recipient must review the notice and any earlier notices for that student and decide whether further action is needed.

Each LEA and public charter school would have to report annually to the Department of Education on information from the preceding school year. Reports must include the number of signs recorded, with counts broken down by who entered them and relevant job or teaching details; counts of students with multiple signs and the number of signs for each such student; and general descriptions of the signs and responses. Reports must not identify students and must comply with the listed privacy laws.

The commissioner of education could withhold an amount of state funds the commissioner determines from an LEA or public charter school that does not comply, until it complies. The system and training requirements, and the notification and review requirements, would not apply to a school system that had a system for documenting students’ early warning signs in place before July 1, 2026, as long as it continues to maintain and use that system.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: These signs include safety, health, or behavioral concerns such as bullying, threats, substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal thoughts.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the general definition and several examples, but omits harassment, intimidation, cyberbullying, and the express coverage of victims and students receiving threats.

assessments.summary_quote: Beginning July 1, 2026, this bill would require each local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to use a computer-based system for teachers and school staff to record students’ “early warning signs.”
assessments.rationale: Conveys the covered entities, required computer-based system, and teacher and staff recording duties. The existing-system exemption is explained later.

assessments.summary_quote: Schools must train teachers and staff to recognize these signs and use the system.
assessments.rationale: Conveys both required training subjects for teachers and staff, with the exemption addressed later.

assessments.summary_quote: The system must align with the specified bullying, discipline, and school safety policies
assessments.rationale: Conveys alignment in the three subject areas, but does not distinguish the required School Discipline Act compliance from policies or identify the required school safety plans.

assessments.summary_quote: The system must align with the specified bullying, discipline, and school safety policies; keep the entered information;
assessments.rationale: Together with the described data-entry system, retaining entered information conveys the database's required receiving and maintenance functions.

assessments.summary_quote: and immediately notify the LEA threat assessment team or a designated charter-school employee when a sign is recorded.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the triggering entry, immediate notification, and both alternative recipients.

assessments.summary_quote: The recipient must review the notice and any earlier notices for that student and decide whether further action is needed.
assessments.rationale: Conveys review of current and previous notifications and the required decision about further action. The exemption is addressed later.

assessments.summary_quote: Each LEA and public charter school would have to report annually to the Department of Education on information from the preceding school year. Reports must include the number of signs recorded
assessments.rationale: Includes the reporting entities, recipient, annual frequency, preceding-school-year period, and total sign count.

assessments.summary_quote: with counts broken down by who entered them and relevant job or teaching details
assessments.rationale: Conveys disaggregation generally, but omits the specific teacher grade-level and subject-area breakdowns and staff position, assignment, and duties breakdowns.

assessments.summary_quote: counts of students with multiple signs and the number of signs for each such student
assessments.rationale: Conveys both the number of students with multiple entries and the number of entries for each such student.

assessments.summary_quote: and general descriptions of the signs and responses. Reports must not identify students and must comply with the listed privacy laws.
assessments.rationale: Conveys general descriptions and nonidentification, but does not specify that responses must be described for each entered sign.
Conveys the report-wide prohibition on information that identifies students.

assessments.summary_quote: Reports must not identify students and must comply with the listed privacy laws.
assessments.rationale: Conveys a privacy-law compliance obligation, but never identifies FERPA, the state confidentiality provision, or the Data Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, and does not expressly cover all other relevant privacy laws.

assessments.summary_quote: The commissioner of education could withhold an amount of state funds the commissioner determines from an LEA or public charter school that does not comply, until it complies.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the commissioner's discretionary withholding authority, covered entities, noncompliance condition, discretion over the amount, and duration.

assessments.summary_quote: The system and training requirements, and the notification and review requirements, would not apply to a school system that had a system for documenting students’ early warning signs in place before July 1, 2026, as long as it continues to maintain and use that system.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the exempt requirements, pre-July 1, 2026 implementation condition, and continued maintenance and use. The separately stated universal reporting duty remains outside this exemption.
